So I don't find that surprising. But I must refer -- return to the question of Glogova 1 and 2. I only know about Glogova 1. Glogova 2 was excavated after I had stopped working for ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But look how it was found. For example, in Glogova 1 there were links of 11 with Budak 1, three with Budak 3, 13 with Bilic 3, three connections with Zeleni Jadar 6, 13 with Zeleni Jadar 5, six with Zeleni Jadar 4, and so on and so forth. So this is absolutely a question of a mixture being found in Glogova 1. But I understand that you would not have been in a position to know that because the DNA tests were not conducted then. But do you agree now that things seem much more complex than they seemed then?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD WRIGHT
utterances.text: I don't know the -- whether I had anything to do with the Budak graves, but I certainly had things to do the Zeleni Jadar graves, and they were secondary graves which contained body parts and which we interpreted as having come from the robbing at Glogova. So in October 1995 bodies why were taken away from Glogova but parts were left behind. Bodies parts were taken away from Glogova and buried in -- at Zeleni Jadar, I've forgotten the number of the grave. We only investigated one. 5, I think. And so I would expect that some body parts from some individuals would be found both in the Glogova and in Zeleni Jadar. But I can't talk about the other sites, Budak 3 and 13 that you mention, because I don't know about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Professor, sir, do you know that some artefacts and some forensic matter was destroyed after they reached this prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD WRIGHT
utterances.text: No. As I said to you, I don't know what happened to the artefacts after I handed them over. I was not in the employment of ICTY. I was under contract to do the graves. So I haven't been following what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Professor, sir, thank you very much for your kindness. Thank you very much for your answers. I apologise if I was not precise. I myself seek to be as precise as possible, and precision is what I'm after, but I would like to thank you very much for your help. I have no more questions for you, sir, because I did not study other documents. I didn't have enough time. But I even think that the ones that I did provide as examples are of use and are instructive. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, Professor Wright. On behalf of this Chamber and the Tribunal as a whole, I would like to thank you for your coming yet again to the Tribunal to give it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll rise all together. Yes, Mr. -- then, Professor, you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, just as we haven't quite run out of time, I wanted to make a brief oral motion which is not opposed. I would tender the errata sheet that Mr. Brown spoke about on the 24th of November at the end of his testimony. We've received an ERN, and it was disclosed a few days ago. It is 65 ter number 90303. And that's the errata sheet prepared based on the questions put to Mr. Brown during his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Should we admit it as a separate Prosecution exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P4028, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are there any matters to deal with? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may just talk about the pace. I am sure for myself that I have not been 25 years old for quite some time now, so this pace, I believe, is quite taxing for everybody in this courtroom, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We are sitting five days a week this week, but we have less than a month until the winter break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And long days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 2nd day of December, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
